newsitem.title: USA: Crews cleaning up oil spill in San Francisco Bay.
newsitem.headline: Crews cleaning up oil spill in San Francisco Bay.

text.p: Crews were working Monday to clean up about 8,400 gallons of oil that spilled from a ship into scenic San Francisco Bay, the Coast Guard said.
The ship, the "Cape Mohegan", was being worked on in a San Francisco dry dock when the bunker oil spilled, Coast Guard spokeswoman Shelly Freier said.
About 20,000 gallons of bunker oil spilled into the dry dock and about 8,400 gallons went into the bay, she said.
She said booms had been placed around the spill but an unknown quantity of oil had seeped out.
Cleanup crews were working to contain the spill and the Coast Guard had pollution investigators on scene, Freier said.

Asked about possible environmental damage, Freier said the spill was moving north into a docklands area and there were no wildlife sanctuaries currently in the line of the spill. The cause of the spill was unknown.
